inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. Organised by hundreds of groups, including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, the Together Alliance event was billed as the biggest [...] The post Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise appeared first on Digital Journal .
inputs.modified_text: This looks less like a spontaneous response and more like a carefully managed political spectacle. Hundreds of groups were involved, and holding the rally weeks before local elections gives the timing a purpose: keep the far-right threat front and centre and steer what voters are allowed to focus on. The “stand against extremism” framing may be the cover; mass rallies can also signal which views are acceptable and funnel public opinion where the organisers want it. I wouldn’t assume this was organic.
